name: aNewSpring
tagline: Dutch learning platform that training companies use to run blended courses, cohorts and adaptive exam prep.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This is not a personal tool, it is infrastructure for organisations that sell training. The thing being paid for is learner administration at scale: cohorts, facilitators, enrolment, certificates, SCORM and xAPI content that was authored elsewhere, and reports someone has to show an auditor or an accreditation body. An agent can absolutely build you a local course player with lessons, quizzes and spaced repetition in a weekend, and if you are a solo learner studying your own material that is genuinely enough. But the moment there is a second person, a paying student, or a regulator, you are rebuilding a multi tenant platform with GDPR commitments and HR system integrations, and that is not a one shot. Build the player if you want the player, do not pretend it replaces the platform.
coreLoopDIY: A local course player: markdown lessons plus quiz questions, progress tracking, and a spaced repetition queue that resurfaces questions you got wrong.
requirements: Node 20 and a local machine or small VPS
Your own lesson content as markdown files
Quiz questions written by you, no imported SCORM packages
whatYouLose: SCORM and xAPI support, so any licensed course package you already own will not load
Cohort and facilitator features: enrolment, deadlines, group pacing, assignment review
Certificates, audit trails and the reporting that accreditation bodies ask for
Integrations with HR, CRM and webshop systems that training providers rely on for signups and billing
Hosted uptime, backups and a data processing agreement someone else signed
moatNotes: Course content, learner history and exam results are the stickiest data in education software. Nobody migrates mid cohort.
whyPeopleStillPay: Training providers are not buying a quiz engine, they are buying the boring administrative spine around it: who is enrolled, who passed, who gets a certificate, which content package came from which publisher, and what the reporting looks like when an auditor asks. That spine is unglamorous, slow to build, and legally consequential if you get it wrong. A single teacher with their own material can self host something decent in a weekend; an organisation with a few hundred active learners and a licensing contract cannot.
notes: A course player for one learner is a weekend build; a training business running cohorts is not. The moat is switching costs on learner records plus the accreditation reporting and HR integrations that training providers are actually paying for.
prompt:
Build a local, single-learner course player. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable:
- Next.js 15 (App Router) with TypeScript and Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/course.db
- Content read from ./content at startup, no CMS, no database-stored lessons

Content format:
- ./content/NN-slug.md per lesson, frontmatter with title, order, optional prerequisites
- ./content/NN-slug.questions.yaml with a list of questions: id, type (multiple-choice or short-answer), prompt, choices, answer, explanation
- On boot, parse content and upsert lessons and questions into SQLite keyed by stable ids

Features that are in scope:
- Lesson list with completion state, and a lesson reader rendering markdown including code blocks
- Quiz runner per lesson: answer, immediate grade, show explanation
- Spaced repetition queue using plain SM-2: each question row stores ease, interval, next_due; a /review page serves whatever is due today across all lessons
- Dashboard: streak, questions due, per lesson accuracy, a simple 30 day activity bar chart
- JSON export and import of all progress at /api/export and /api/import

Explicitly out of scope, do not build:
- Users, auth, roles, cohorts, invites
- SCORM or xAPI import, certificates, payments, email
- Any external API calls at all

Details:
- Secrets: none needed, but create .env.example anyway with PORT only
- Seed ./content with three short sample lessons and five questions each so the app works on first run
- Include a README with run instructions and the exact content file schema
- Add a single vitest file covering the SM-2 scheduling math and the content parser
- Everything must work offline after npm install
